123	class DatasetCatalog:
124	    def __init__(self, path):
125	        self.path = Path(path)
126	
127	    def entries(self):
128	        return json.loads(self.path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if self.path.exists() else {}
129	
130	    def _normalize_entry(self, dataset, known_ids):
131	        return _normalized_record(dataset, known_ids)
132	
133	    def register(self, dataset):
134	        records = self.entries()
135	        if not isinstance(dataset, dict):
136	            raise ValueError("invalid dataset descriptor")
137	        identifier = dataset.get("id")
138	        if not isinstance(identifier, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*", identifier):
139	            raise ValueError("invalid dataset id")
140	        if identifier in records:
141	            raise ValueError("dataset already registered")
142	        entry = self._normalize_entry(dataset, set(records))
143	        records[identifier] = entry
144	        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
145	        self.path.write_text(json.dumps(records, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
146	        return entry
147	
148	    def describe(self, identifier):
149	        records = self.entries()
150	        if identifier not in records:
151	            raise ValueError("unknown dataset")
152	        return records[identifier]
153	
154	    def search(self, query="", field_type=None, tags=None, owner=None):
155	        if not isinstance(query, str):
156	            raise ValueError("query must be a string")
157	        if field_type is not None and field_type not in FIELD_TYPES:
158	            raise ValueError("field_type must be None or one of string, integer, number, boolean")
159	        required_tags = _normalize_tags(tags) if tags is not None else []
160	        required_owner = _normalize_owner(owner).casefold() if owner is not None else None
161	        words = {word.casefold() for word in query.split()}
162	        records = self.entries()
163	        results = []
164	        for identifier in sorted(records):
165	            entry = records[identifier]
166	            if field_type is not None and not any(field["type"] == field_type for field in entry["fields"]):
167	                continue
168	            if required_tags:
169	                available = {tag.casefold() for tag in entry.get("tags", [])}
170	                if not all(tag.casefold() in available for tag in required_tags):
171	                    continue
172	            if required_owner is not None:
173	                entry_owner = entry.get("owner")
174	                if not isinstance(entry_owner, str) or entry_owner.casefold() != required_owner:
175	                    continue
176	            matched_indices = set()
177	            matched = True
178	            dataset_haystack = (entry["id"] + "\n" + entry.get("description", "")).casefold()
179	            for word in words:
180	                hits = {index for index, field in enumerate(entry["fields"])
181	                        if word in field["name"].casefold()}
182	                matched_indices.update(hits)
183	                if not hits and word not in dataset_haystack:
184	                    matched = False
185	                    break
186	            if matched:
187	                results.append({"dataset": entry,
188	                                "matched_fields": [entry["fields"][index]["name"]
189	                                                   for index in sorted(matched_indices)]})
190	        return results
191	
192	    def dependencies(self, identifier):
193	        entry = self.describe(identifier)
194	        return [self.describe(key) for key in entry["depends_on"]]
195	
196	    def impact(self, identifier, max_depth=None):
197	        if max_depth is not None and (isinstance(max_depth, bool)
198	                                      or not isinstance(max_depth, int) or max_depth <= 0):
199	            raise ValueError("max_depth must be None or a positive integer")
200	        records = self.entries()
201	        if identifier not in records:
202	            raise ValueError("unknown dataset")
203	        downstream = {}
204	        for key, entry in records.items():
205	            for source in entry["depends_on"]:
206	                downstream.setdefault(source, set()).add(key)
207	        reached = {identifier: [identifier]}
208	        frontier = {identifier: [identifier]}
209	        result = []
210	        distance = 0
211	        while frontier and (max_depth is None or distance < max_depth):
212	            distance += 1
213	            candidates = {}
214	            for node, path in frontier.items():
215	                for child in downstream.get(node, ()):  # unconnected records are never reached
216	                    if child in reached:
217	                        continue
218	                    candidate = path + [child]
219	                    if child not in candidates or candidate < candidates[child]:
220	                        candidates[child] = candidate
221	            if not candidates:
222	                break
223	            frontier = candidates
224	            reached.update(candidates)
225	            for child, path in candidates.items():
226	                result.append({"dataset": records[child], "distance": distance, "path": path})
227	        result.sort(key=lambda item: (item["distance"], item["dataset"]["id"]))
228	        return result
229	
230	    def export(self, identifiers=None):
231	        if identifiers is not None and not isinstance(identifiers, list):
232	            raise ValueError("identifiers must be None or a list of dataset ids")
233	        selected = []
234	        if identifiers is not None:
235	            for item in identifiers:
236	                if not isinstance(item, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*", item):
237	                    raise ValueError("invalid dataset id")
238	                if item not in selected:
239	                    selected.append(item)
240	        records = self.entries()
241	        unknown = [item for item in selected if item not in records]
242	        if unknown:
243	            raise ValueError("unknown dataset")
244	        if identifiers is None:
245	            selected = list(records)
246	
247	        included = set()
248	        stack = list(selected)
249	        while stack:
250	            key = stack.pop()
251	            if key in included:
252	                continue
253	            included.add(key)
254	            for source in records[key]["depends_on"]:
255	                if source not in records:
256	                    raise ValueError("missing dependency")
257	                if source not in included:
258	                    stack.append(source)
259	
260	        subset = {key: records[key] for key in included}
261	        ordered = _toposort(subset)
262	        if ordered is None:
263	            raise ValueError("dependency cycle detected")
264	        return {"datasets": [records[key] for key in ordered]}
265	
266	    def import_bundle(self, bundle):
267	        if not isinstance(bundle, dict):
268	            raise ValueError("bundle must be an object")
269	        descriptors = bundle.get("datasets")
270	        if not isinstance(descriptors, list):
271	            raise ValueError("bundle must contain a datasets array")
272	
273	        records = self.entries()
274	        batch_ids = set()
275	        for dataset in descriptors:
276	            if not isinstance(dataset, dict):
277	                raise ValueError("invalid dataset descriptor")
278	            identifier = dataset.get("id")
279	            if not isinstance(identifier, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*", identifier):
280	                raise ValueError("invalid dataset id")
281	            if identifier in records or identifier in batch_ids:
282	                raise ValueError("dataset already registered")
283	            batch_ids.add(identifier)
284	
285	        known = set(records) | batch_ids
286	        new_entries = {}
287	        for dataset in descriptors:
288	            entry = self._normalize_entry(dataset, known)
289	            if entry["id"] in entry["depends_on"]:
290	                raise ValueError("dependencies must be unique, already registered dataset ids")
291	            new_entries[entry["id"]] = entry
292	
293	        batch = {key: {"depends_on": [dep for dep in entry["depends_on"] if dep in batch_ids]}
294	                 for key, entry in new_entries.items()}
295	        ordered = _toposort(batch)
296	        if ordered is None:
297	            raise ValueError("dependency cycle detected")
298	
299	        imported = [new_entries[key] for key in ordered]
300	        if new_entries:
301	            for entry in imported:
302	                records[entry["id"]] = entry
303	            self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
304	            self.path.write_text(json.dumps(records, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n",
305	                                 encoding="utf-8")
306	        return {"datasets": imported}
307	
308	    def _snapshot_state(self, bundle):
309	        if not isinstance(bundle, dict):
310	            raise ValueError("bundle must be an object")
311	        descriptors = bundle.get("datasets")
312	        if not isinstance(descriptors, list):
313	            raise ValueError("bundle must contain a datasets array")
314	
315	        snapshot_ids = set()
316	        for dataset in descriptors:
317	            if not isinstance(dataset, dict):
318	                raise ValueError("invalid dataset descriptor")
319	            identifier = dataset.get("id")
320	            if not isinstance(identifier, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*", identifier):
321	                raise ValueError("invalid dataset id")
322	            if identifier in snapshot_ids:
323	                raise ValueError("dataset already registered")
324	            snapshot_ids.add(identifier)
325	
326	        snapshot = {}
327	        for dataset in descriptors:
328	            entry = _normalized_record(dataset, snapshot_ids)
329	            if entry["id"] in entry["depends_on"]:
330	                raise ValueError("dependencies must be unique, already registered dataset ids")
331	            snapshot[entry["id"]] = entry
332	        if _toposort(snapshot) is None:
333	            raise ValueError("dependency cycle detected")
334	        return snapshot
335	
336	    @staticmethod
337	    def _diff_states(current, snapshot):
338	        before_ids = set(current)
339	        after_ids = set(snapshot)
340	        added = [copy.deepcopy(snapshot[key]) for key in sorted(after_ids - before_ids)]
341	        removed = [copy.deepcopy(current[key]) for key in sorted(before_ids - after_ids)]
342	        changed = []
343	        for key in sorted(before_ids & after_ids):
344	            before = current[key]
345	            after = snapshot[key]
346	            changed_keys = sorted(name for name in set(before) | set(after)
347	                                  if before.get(name) != after.get(name))
348	            if changed_keys:
349	                changed.append({"id": key, "before": copy.deepcopy(before),
350	                                "after": copy.deepcopy(after), "changed_keys": changed_keys})
351	        return {"added": added, "removed": removed, "changed": changed}
352	
353	    def diff_bundle(self, bundle):
354	        snapshot = self._snapshot_state(bundle)
355	        records = self.entries()
356	        current = {key: _normalized_record(entry, set(records))
357	                   for key, entry in records.items()}
358	        return self._diff_states(current, snapshot)
359	
360	    def _current_state(self):
361	        records = self.entries()
362	        if not isinstance(records, dict):
363	            raise ValueError("invalid catalog state")
364	        current = {}
365	        for key, entry in records.items():
366	            normalized = _normalized_record(entry, set(records))
367	            if normalized["id"] != key:
368	                raise ValueError("invalid dataset descriptor")
369	            if normalized["id"] in normalized["depends_on"]:
370	                raise ValueError("dependencies must be unique, already registered dataset ids")
371	            current[key] = normalized
372	        if _toposort(current) is None:
373	            raise ValueError("dependency cycle detected")
374	        return current
375	
376	    def preview_bundle(self, bundle):
377	        snapshot = self._snapshot_state(bundle)
378	        current = self._current_state()
379	
380	        diff = self._diff_states(current, snapshot)
381	        sources = {row["id"] for row in diff["added"]}
382	        sources.update(row["id"] for row in diff["removed"])
383	        sources.update(row["id"] for row in diff["changed"])
384	
385	        # target id -> source id -> {"before"/"after": propagation explanation}
386	        reached_by = {}
387	        for side, state in (("before", current), ("after", snapshot)):
388	            downstream = _downstream_index(state)
389	            for source in sources:
390	                if source not in state:
391	                    continue
392	                for target, path in _shortest_downstream_paths(downstream, source).items():
393	                    propagation = {"distance": len(path) - 1, "path": path}
394	                    reached_by.setdefault(target, {}).setdefault(source, {})[side] = propagation
395	
396	        affected = []
397	        for target in sorted(reached_by):
398	            causes = []
399	            for source in sorted(reached_by[target]):
400	                sides = reached_by[target][source]
401	                before = sides.get("before")
402	                after = sides.get("after")
403	                if before is None and after is None:
404	                    continue
405	                causes.append({"id": source, "before": before, "after": after})
406	            if causes:
407	                affected.append({"id": target, "causes": causes})
408	        return {"diff": diff, "affected": affected}
409	
410	    def _save_records(self, records):
411	        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
412	        data = json.dumps(records, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n"
413	        fd, temp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=str(self.path.parent),
414	                                         prefix=self.path.name + ".", suffix=".tmp")
415	        try:
416	            with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
417	                handle.write(data)
418	            os.replace(temp_name, self.path)
419	        except BaseException:
420	            try:
421	                os.unlink(temp_name)
422	            except OSError:
423	                pass
424	            raise
425	
426	    def apply_bundle(self, bundle, expected_bundle=None):
427	        snapshot = self._snapshot_state(bundle)
428	        expected = None if expected_bundle is None else self._snapshot_state(expected_bundle)
429	        current = self._current_state()
430	        if expected is not None and current != expected:
431	            raise ValueError("catalog does not match expected snapshot")
432	        diff = self._diff_states(current, snapshot)
433	        if diff["added"] or diff["removed"] or diff["changed"]:
434	            ordered = _toposort(snapshot)
435	            self._save_records({key: snapshot[key] for key in ordered})
436	        return diff

442	    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

import json
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from unittest import mock
from dataset_catalog import DatasetCatalog

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent


class CatalogTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT)
        self.addCleanup(self.temp.cleanup)
        self.path = Path(self.temp.name) / "catalog.json"
        self.catalog = DatasetCatalog(self.path)
        self.raw = {"id": "orders", "fields": [{"name": "amount", "type": "number"}]}

    def test_register_persists_schema_and_direct_dependencies(self):
        self.catalog.register(self.raw)
        self.catalog.register({"id": "daily", "fields": [{"name": "total", "type": "number"}], "depends_on": ["orders"]})
        self.catalog.register({"id": "weekly", "fields": [{"name": "total", "type": "number"}], "depends_on": ["daily"]})
        fresh = DatasetCatalog(self.path)
        self.assertEqual([row["id"] for row in fresh.dependencies("weekly")], ["daily"])
        self.assertEqual(fresh.describe("orders")["fields"], self.raw["fields"])

    def test_bad_dependencies_and_duplicate_fields_do_not_write(self):
        for item in ({**self.raw, "depends_on": ["unknown"]}, {**self.raw, "fields": self.raw["fields"] * 2}):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                self.catalog.register(item)
        self.assertFalse(self.path.exists())

    def test_duplicate_and_unknown_dataset(self):
        self.catalog.register(self.raw)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.catalog.register(self.raw)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.catalog.dependencies("missing")

    def _register(self, identifier, depends_on=None):
        self.catalog.register({"id": identifier,
                               "fields": [{"name": "n", "type": "integer"}],
                               "depends_on": depends_on or []})

    def test_impact_lists_reachable_downstream_with_shortest_paths(self):
        for identifier, depends_on in (("orders", []), ("daily", ["orders"]),
                                       ("weekly", ["daily"]), ("report", ["orders"])):
            self._register(identifier, depends_on)
        result = self.catalog.impact("orders")
        self.assertEqual([(row["dataset"]["id"], row["distance"], row["path"]) for row in result],
                         [("daily", 1, ["orders", "daily"]),
                          ("report", 1, ["orders", "report"]),
                          ("weekly", 2, ["orders", "daily", "weekly"])])

    def test_impact_respects_max_depth_and_empty_leaf(self):
        for identifier, depends_on in (("orders", []), ("daily", ["orders"]),
                                       ("weekly", ["daily"])):
            self._register(identifier, depends_on)
        self.assertEqual([row["dataset"]["id"] for row in self.catalog.impact("orders", 1)], ["daily"])
        self.assertEqual(self.catalog.impact("weekly"), [])

    def test_impact_picks_lexicographically_smallest_shortest_path(self):
        for identifier, depends_on in (("orders", []), ("b", ["orders"]), ("c", ["orders"]),
                                       ("d", ["c", "b"])):
            self._register(identifier, depends_on)
        result = self.catalog.impact("orders")
        self.assertEqual([row["dataset"]["id"] for row in result], ["b", "c", "d"])
        self.assertEqual(result[-1]["path"], ["orders", "b", "d"])

    def test_impact_rejects_invalid_max_depth_and_unknown_source(self):
        self._register("orders")
        for bad in (True, False, 0, -1, 1.0, "1"):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                self.catalog.impact("orders", bad)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.catalog.impact("missing")

    def test_cli_impact(self):
        prefix = [sys.executable, str(ROOT / "dataset_catalog.py"), "--catalog", str(self.path)]
        subprocess.run(prefix + ["register", str(ROOT / "samples/orders.json")], check=True, capture_output=True)
        subprocess.run(prefix + ["register", str(ROOT / "samples/daily.json")], check=True, capture_output=True)
        ok = subprocess.run(prefix + ["impact", "orders"], capture_output=True, text=True)
        self.assertEqual(ok.returncode, 0, ok.stderr)
        result = json.loads(ok.stdout)
        self.assertEqual([row["dataset"]["id"] for row in result], ["daily_totals"])
        self.assertEqual(result[0]["distance"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(result[0]["path"], ["orders", "daily_totals"])
        self.assertEqual(subprocess.run(prefix + ["impact", "orders", "--max-depth", "0"],
                                       capture_output=True, text=True).returncode, 2)
        depth_error = subprocess.run(prefix + ["impact", "missing", "--max-depth", "x"],
                                     capture_output=True, text=True)
        self.assertEqual(depth_error.returncode, 2)
        self.assertIn("error", json.loads(depth_error.stdout))
        self.assertEqual(subprocess.run(prefix + ["impact", "missing"],
                                        capture_output=True).returncode, 2)

    def test_cli_query_and_registration(self):
        prefix = [sys.executable, str(ROOT / "dataset_catalog.py"), "--catalog", str(self.path)]
        run = subprocess.run(prefix + ["register", str(ROOT / "samples/orders.json")], capture_output=True, text=True)
        self.assertEqual(run.returncode, 0, run.stderr)
        query = subprocess.run(prefix + ["describe", "orders"], capture_output=True, text=True)
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(query.stdout)["id"], "orders")
        self.assertEqual(subprocess.run(prefix + ["describe", "missing"], capture_output=True).returncode, 2)

    def _chain(self):
        for identifier, depends_on in (("orders", []), ("daily_totals", ["orders"]),
                                       ("weekly", ["daily_totals"]), ("report", ["orders"])):
            self._register(identifier, depends_on)

    def test_export_all_orders_dependencies_before_dependents(self):
        self._chain()
        result = self.catalog.export()
        self.assertEqual(set(result), {"datasets"})
        ids = [row["id"] for row in result["datasets"]]
        self.assertEqual(ids.index("orders"), 0)
        self.assertLess(ids.index("daily_totals"), ids.index("weekly"))
        self.assertEqual([row["id"] for row in self.catalog.export([])["datasets"]], [])

    def test_export_selected_includes_only_upstream_closure(self):
        self._chain()
        ids = [row["id"] for row in self.catalog.export(["daily_totals"])["datasets"]]
        self.assertEqual(ids, ["orders", "daily_totals"])
        self.assertEqual([row["id"] for row in self.catalog.export(["orders"])["datasets"]], ["orders"])
        ids = [row["id"] for row in self.catalog.export(["report", "weekly", "weekly"])["datasets"]]
        self.assertEqual(ids, ["orders", "daily_totals", "report", "weekly"])
        ids = [row["id"] for row in self.catalog.export(["weekly", "report"])["datasets"]]

    def _snapshot_record(self, identifier, depends_on=None, tags=..., description=...,
                         fields=None):
        record = {"id": identifier,
                  "description": identifier + " desc" if description is ... else description,
                  "fields": fields or [{"name": "n", "type": "integer"}],
                  "depends_on": depends_on or []}
        if tags is not ... and tags is not None:
            record["tags"] = tags
        return record

An empty or whitespace-only query imposes no keyword restriction; when `field_type` is one of string, integer, number or boolean the dataset must have at least one field of that type while keywords still search every field name. A non-string query, or a `field_type` other than `None` and the four supported types, raises `ValueError` — arguments are validated before the catalog is read, so a missing or empty catalog still yields `[]` and never creates a file. `DatasetCatalog.search(query="", field_type=None, tags=None, owner=None)` also accepts `tags`: `None` or `[]` imposes no tag restriction, while a nonempty list requires the dataset to carry every listed tag. Records registered before owners existed are treated as having no owner and are never rewritten by a search. Keyword, field-type, tag and owner conditions all apply together; keywords still search only the original scopes (owner is not a keyword scope) and `matched_fields` still reflects keyword hits only. The call never mutates the bundle, catalog or snapshot file, never creates files or directories, and never reads dataset contents; the output is independent of input order. `DatasetCatalog.apply_bundle(bundle, expected_bundle=None)` commits a validated snapshot bundle as the complete catalog state — same-id records are replaced, new ids are added, records missing from the snapshot are removed, and an empty snapshot clears the catalog — and returns the pre-commit diff exactly as `diff_bundle` would have returned it (the `added`/`removed`/`changed` arrays sorted by id, with full before/after records and `changed_keys`). Normalization and snapshot validation match `diff_bundle`, the current catalog is validated with `preview_bundle`'s rules, and a missing catalog file or `{}` is an empty before state; any validation failure raises `ValueError` before anything is written, so the catalog file keeps its original contents and a missing file or its parent directories are never created. The commit is all-or-nothing: with differences the full set of normalized records is saved atomically in the existing storage format (parent directories are created as needed), a save failure raises `OSError` leaving the original file untouched and a previously missing file still absent, and an empty diff returns the three empty arrays without writing a file or creating directories. When `expected_bundle` is not `None` it is validated with the same snapshot rules as the target and compared against the current catalog read for this call — normalized records aligned by dataset id, ignoring dataset order, object key order, unsaved properties and dependency order, while field order, tag retention/spelling/order and cleaned owner spelling count; a mismatch raises `ValueError("catalog does not match expected snapshot")` before anything is written, even when the target equals the current state, and an empty expected snapshot matches only an empty catalog. The call never mutates the passed bundle, mutating the returned records affects neither the input nor the saved catalog, and afterwards `describe`, `dependencies`, `search`, `impact` and `export` immediately reflect the new state; existing registration, import, export, diff and preview behavior is unchanged. `DatasetCatalog.search(query="", field_type=None)` is read-only and returns a list sorted by dataset id; each item holds the same full record as `describe` under `dataset` and `matched_fields`, the field names hit by any query word in original field order without duplicates (empty when no field is hit or the query is empty). The query is split on Unicode whitespace, duplicate words do not change the result, and matching is literal substring matching after Unicode casefold — no regex or wildcards; every word must hit the same dataset, possibly across its id, description and different field names. An empty or whitespace-only query imposes no keyword restriction; when `field_type` is one of string, integer, number or boolean the dataset must have at least one field of that type while keywords still search every field name. A non-string query, or a `field_type` other than `None` and the four supported types, raises `ValueError` — arguments are validated before the catalog is read, so a missing or empty catalog still yields `[]` and never creates a file. `DatasetCatalog.search(query="", field_type=None, tags=None, owner=None)` also accepts `tags`: `None` or `[]` imposes no tag restriction, while a nonempty list requires the dataset to carry every listed tag. Tags follow the same type, stripping and dedup rules as registration, are validated before the catalog is read, and match whole tags by Unicode casefold only — no word splitting, substring, regex or wildcard matching. `owner=None` imposes no owner restriction; any other value is stripped of surrounding Unicode whitespace under the same nonempty-string rules as registration and must equal the record's stored owner in full after Unicode casefold — no word splitting, substring or wildcard matching. Records without an owner never match an owner filter; the owner filter is validated before the catalog is read. Records registered before owners existed are treated as having no owner and are never rewritten by a search. Keyword, field-type, tag and owner conditions all apply together; keywords still search only the original scopes (owner is not a keyword scope) and `matched_fields` still reflects keyword hits only. CLI errors are JSON and exit 2. Run `python3 -B -m unittest -v` for persistence, dependency validation and CLI tests.

def _schema_record(self, identifier, fields, depends_on=None, description="s", **extra):
        record = {"id": identifier, "description": description,
                  "fields": fields, "depends_on": depends_on or []}
        record.update(extra)
        return record

    def test_schema_diff_add_remove_and_type_change_structure(self):
        self.catalog.import_bundle({"datasets": [
            self._schema_record("a", [{"name": "keep", "type": "string"},
                                      {"name": "gone", "type": "integer"},
                                      {"name": "widened", "type": "integer"},
                                      {"name": "narrowed", "type": "number"},
                                      {"name": "switched", "type": "string"}]),
            self._schema_record("b", [{"name": "n", "type": "integer"}], ["a"])]})
        bundle = {"datasets": [
            self._schema_record("a", [{"name": "fresh", "type": "boolean"},
                                      {"name": "keep", "type": "string"},
                                      {"name": "widened", "type": "number"},
                                      {"name": "narrowed", "type": "integer"},
                                      {"name": "switched", "type": "boolean"}]),
            self._schema_record("b", [{"name": "n", "type": "integer"}], ["a"])]}
        result = self.catalog.schema_diff_bundle(bundle)
        self.assertEqual(set(result), {"changes"})
        self.assertEqual([row["id"] for row in result["changes"]], ["a"])
        change = result["changes"][0]
        self.assertEqual(set(change),
                         {"id", "added_fields", "removed_fields", "type_changes", "breaking"})
        self.assertEqual(change["added_fields"], [{"name": "fresh", "type": "boolean"}])
        self.assertEqual(change["removed_fields"], [{"name": "gone", "type": "integer"}])
        self.assertEqual(change["type_changes"], [
            {"name": "narrowed", "before": "number", "after": "integer"},
            {"name": "switched", "before": "string", "after": "boolean"},
            {"name": "widened", "before": "integer", "after": "number"}])
        self.assertIs(change["breaking"], True)

    def test_schema_diff_integer_to_number_is_not_breaking(self):
        self.catalog.import_bundle({"datasets": [
            self._schema_record("a", [{"name": "x", "type": "integer"},
                                      {"name": "y", "type": "integer"},
                                      {"name": "z", "type": "string"}])]})
        bundle = {"datasets": [
            self._schema_record("a", [{"name": "x", "type": "number"},
                                      {"name": "y", "type": "integer"},
                                      {"name": "z", "type": "string"}])]}
        change = self.catalog.schema_diff_bundle(bundle)["changes"]
        self.assertEqual(len(change), 1)
        self.assertEqual(change[0]["added_fields"], [])
        self.assertEqual(change[0]["removed_fields"], [])
        self.assertEqual(change[0]["type_changes"],
                         [{"name": "x", "before": "integer", "after": "number"}])
        self.assertIs(change[0]["breaking"], False)

        for before_type, after_type in (("number", "integer"), ("string", "integer"),
                                        ("integer", "string"), ("boolean", "string"),
                                        ("string", "boolean"), ("number", "string")):
            other = Path(self.temp.name) / ("types-" + before_type + "-" + after_type + ".json")
            catalog = DatasetCatalog(other)
            catalog.import_bundle({"datasets": [
                self._schema_record("a", [{"name": "f", "type": before_type}])]})
            row = catalog.schema_diff_bundle({"datasets": [
                self._schema_record("a", [{"name": "f", "type": after_type}])]})["changes"][0]
            self.assertIs(row["breaking"], True, (before_type, after_type))
            self.assertEqual(row["type_changes"],
                             [{"name": "f", "before": before_type, "after": after_type}])

    def test_schema_diff_new_dataset_all_added_and_deleted_all_removed(self):
        self.catalog.import_bundle({"datasets": [
            self._schema_record("old", [{"name": "a", "type": "integer"},
                                        {"name": "b", "type": "string"}])]})
        result = self.catalog.schema_diff_bundle({"datasets": [
            self._schema_record("old", [{"name": "a", "type": "integer"},
                                        {"name": "b", "type": "string"}]),
            self._schema_record("new", [{"name": "x", "type": "number"},
                                        {"name": "y", "type": "boolean"}], ["old"])]})
        changes = result["changes"]
        self.assertEqual([row["id"] for row in changes], ["new", "old"])
        added_only, deleted_only = changes
        self.assertEqual(added_only["added_fields"],
                         [{"name": "x", "type": "number"}, {"name": "y", "type": "boolean"}])
        self.assertEqual(added_only["removed_fields"], [])
        self.assertEqual(added_only["type_changes"], [])
        self.assertIs(added_only["breaking"], False)
        # deleting a dataset means all its fields are removed
        empty = self.catalog.schema_diff_bundle({"datasets": []})["changes"]
        self.assertEqual(len(empty), 1)
        self.assertEqual(empty[0]["id"], "old")
        self.assertEqual(empty[0]["added_fields"], [])
        self.assertEqual(empty[0]["type_changes"], [])
        self.assertEqual(empty[0]["removed_fields"],
                         [{"name": "a", "type": "integer"}, {"name": "b", "type": "string"}])
        self.assertIs(empty[0]["breaking"], True)

    def test_schema_diff_arrays_sorted_by_unicode_codepoint(self):
        fields = [{"name": name, "type": "string"}
                  for name in ("b", "a", "A", "B", "01", "日", "é", "abc")]
        self.catalog.import_bundle({"datasets": [self._schema_record("a", fields)]})
        result = self.catalog.schema_diff_bundle({"datasets": [
            self._schema_record("a", [])]})
        removed = [row["name"] for row in result["changes"][0]["removed_fields"]]
        self.assertEqual(removed, sorted(removed))
        self.assertEqual(removed, ["01", "A", "B", "a", "abc", "b", "é", "日"])

        other = Path(self.temp.name) / "unicode-add.json"
        catalog = DatasetCatalog(other)
        after = [{"name": name, "type": "integer"} for name in ("中", "Z", "a", " ")]
        changes = catalog.schema_diff_bundle({"datasets": [
            self._schema_record("a", after)]})["changes"]
        added = [row["name"] for row in changes[0]["added_fields"]]
        self.assertEqual(added, [" ", "Z", "a", "中"])
        self.assertEqual(changes[0]["added_fields"][0], {"name": " ", "type": "integer"})

    def test_schema_diff_rename_is_remove_plus_add_and_matches_names_exactly(self):
        self.catalog.import_bundle({"datasets": [
            self._schema_record("a", [{"name": "Amount", "type": "integer"},
                                      {"name": " id ", "type": "string"}])]})
        bundle = {"datasets": [
            self._schema_record("a", [{"name": "amount", "type": "integer"},
                                      {"name": "id", "type": "string"}])]}
        change = self.catalog.schema_diff_bundle(bundle)["changes"][0]
        self.assertEqual(change["added_fields"], [{"name": "amount", "type": "integer"},
                                                  {"name": "id", "type": "string"}])
        self.assertEqual(change["removed_fields"], [{"name": " Amount", "type": "integer"}[:-7]
                                                    if False else
                                                    {"name": "Amount", "type": "integer"},
                                                    {"name": " id ", "type": "string"}])
        self.assertEqual(change["type_changes"], [])
        self.assertIs(change["breaking"], True)

        # case-only or whitespace-only differences never line up as type changes
        other = Path(self.temp.name) / "exact.json"
        catalog = DatasetCatalog(other)
        catalog.import_bundle({"datasets": [
            self._schema_record("a", [{"name": "x", "type": "integer"}])]})
        row = catalog.schema_diff_bundle({"datasets": [
            self._schema_record("a", [{"name": "x", "type": "integer"},
                                      {"name": "x ", "type": "number"}])]})["changes"][0]
        self.assertEqual(row["added_fields"], [{"name": "x ", "type": "number"}])
        self.assertEqual(row["type_changes"], [])

    def test_schema_diff_ignores_metadata_and_field_order_but_diff_keeps_order_rule(self):
        records = {"datasets": [
            self._schema_record("a", [{"name": "z", "type": "integer"},
                                      {"name": "n", "type": "integer"}], ["b"],
                                tags=["t"], owner="team"),
            self._schema_record("b", [{"name": "n", "type": "integer"}])]}
        self.catalog.import_bundle(records)
        changed = {"datasets": [
            self._schema_record("b", [{"name": "n", "type": "integer"}], description="new desc"),
            self._schema_record("a", [{"name": "n", "type": "integer"},
                                      {"name": "z", "type": "integer"}], ["b"],
                                description="other", tags=["u"], owner="other-team")]}
        self.assertEqual(self.catalog.schema_diff_bundle(changed), {"changes": []})
        # the legacy diff still treats a pure field reorder as a change
        self.assertEqual(
            [row["changed_keys"] for row in self.catalog.diff_bundle(changed)["changed"]],
            [["description", "fields", "owner", "tags"]])

        reordered_only = {"datasets": [
            self._schema_record("a", [{"name": "n", "type": "integer"},
                                      {"name": "z", "type": "integer"}], ["b"],
                                tags=["t"], owner="team"),
            self._schema_record("b")]}
        self.assertEqual(self.catalog.schema_diff_bundle(reordered_only), {"changes": []})
        self.assertEqual(
            [row["changed_keys"] for row in self.catalog.diff_bundle(reordered_only)["changed"]],
            [["fields"]])

    def test_schema_diff_empty_arrays_preserved_on_field_change_only(self):
        self.catalog.import_bundle({"datasets": [
            self._schema_record("a", [{"name": "n", "type": "integer"}])]})
        change = self.catalog.schema_diff_bundle({"datasets": [
            self._schema_record("a", [{"name": "n", "type": "number"}])]})["changes"][0]
        self.assertEqual(change["added_fields"], [])
        self.assertEqual(change["removed_fields"], [])
        self.assertEqual(change["type_changes"],
                         [{"name": "n", "before": "integer", "after": "number"}])
        self.assertIs(change["breaking"], False)

    def test_schema_diff_changes_sorted_by_id_and_unchanged_omitted(self):
        self.catalog.import_bundle({"datasets": [
            self._schema_record("a", [{"name": "n", "type": "integer"}]),
            self._schema_record("b", [{"name": "n", "type": "integer"}]),
            self._schema_record("c", [{"name": "n", "type": "integer"}])]})
        result = self.catalog.schema_diff_bundle({"datasets": [
            self._schema_record("a", [{"name": "n", "type": "string"}]),
            self._schema_record("b", [{"name": "n", "type": "integer"}]),
            self._schema_record("c", [{"name": "n", "type": "integer"},
                                      {"name": "x", "type": "boolean"}])]})
        self.assertEqual([row["id"] for row in result["changes"]], ["a", "c"])

    def test_schema_diff_missing_or_empty_catalog_and_empty_snapshot(self):
        self.assertFalse(self.path.exists())
        result = self.catalog.schema_diff_bundle({"datasets": [
            self._schema_record("a", [{"name": "n", "type": "integer"}])]})
        self.assertEqual([row["id"] for row in result["changes"]], ["a"])
        self.assertEqual(result["changes"][0]["added_fields"],
                         [{"name": "n", "type": "integer"}])
        self.assertFalse(self.path.exists())

        self.path.write_text("{}", encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertEqual(DatasetCatalog(self.path).schema_diff_bundle({"datasets": []}),
                         {"changes": []})

        self.catalog.import_bundle({"datasets": [
            self._schema_record("a", [{"name": "n", "type": "integer"}])]})
        self.assertEqual(self.catalog.schema_diff_bundle({"datasets": []})["changes"][0]["id"], "a")

    def test_schema_diff_validates_both_graphs_even_for_metadata_only_changes(self):
        self.catalog.register(self._snapshot_record("old"))
        bad_bundles = [
            [], None, "x", 1, True, {},
            {"datasets": None}, {"datasets": {}}, {"datasets": "x"}, {"datasets": 1},
            {"other": []},
            {"datasets": [None]},
            {"datasets": ["x"]},
            {"datasets": [{"id": "bad id", "fields": [{"name": "n", "type": "integer"}]}]},
            {"datasets": [{"id": "a"}]},
            {"datasets": [{"id": "a", "fields": [{"name": "n", "type": "float"}]}]},
            {"datasets": [self._snapshot_record("a"), self._snapshot_record("a")]},
            {"datasets": [self._snapshot_record("a", ["a"])]},
            {"datasets": [self._snapshot_record("a", ["b", "b"])]},
            {"datasets": [self._snapshot_record("a", ["ghost"])]},
            {"datasets": [self._snapshot_record("a", ["b"]), self._snapshot_record("b", ["a"])]},
            {"datasets": [self._snapshot_record("a", tags=[""])]},
        ]
        for bundle in bad_bundles:
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                self.catalog.schema_diff_bundle(bundle)

        # validation runs even when no field would change
        harmless = {"datasets": [self._snapshot_record("old", description="changed")]}
        for bundle in bad_bundles[5:]:
            other = Path(self.temp.name) / "bad-schema-snapshot.json"
            catalog = DatasetCatalog(other)
            catalog.register(self._snapshot_record("old"))
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                catalog.schema_diff_bundle(bundle)

        # an invalid current catalog is rejected like in preview
        good = json.dumps({"datasets": [self._snapshot_record("a")]})
        bad_states = [
            json.dumps([self._snapshot_record("a")]),
            json.dumps({"a": "x"}),
            json.dumps({"a": self._snapshot_record("a", ["ghost"])}),
            json.dumps({"a": self._snapshot_record("a", ["a"])}),

def _schema_record(self, identifier, fields, depends_on=None, description="s", **extra):
        record = {"id": identifier, "description": description,
                  "fields": fields, "depends_on": depends_on or []}
        record.update(extra)
        return record

    def test_schema_diff_add_remove_and_type_change_structure(self):
        self.catalog.import_bundle({"datasets": [
            self._schema_record("a", [{"name": "keep", "type": "string"},
                                      {"name": "gone", "type": "integer"},
                                      {"name": "widened", "type": "integer"},
                                      {"name": "narrowed", "type": "number"},
                                      {"name": "switched", "type": "string"}]),
            self._schema_record("b", [{"name": "n", "type": "integer"}], ["a"])]})
        bundle = {"datasets": [
            self._schema_record("a", [{"name": "fresh", "type": "boolean"},
                                      {"name": "keep", "type": "string"},
                                      {"name": "widened", "type": "number"},
                                      {"name": "narrowed", "type": "integer"},
                                      {"name": "switched", "type": "boolean"}]),
            self._schema_record("b", [{"name": "n", "type": "integer"}], ["a"])]}
        result = self.catalog.schema_diff_bundle(bundle)
        self.assertEqual(set(result), {"changes"})
        self.assertEqual([row["id"] for row in result["changes"]], ["a"])
        change = result["changes"][0]
        self.assertEqual(set(change),
                         {"id", "added_fields", "removed_fields", "type_changes", "breaking"})
        self.assertEqual(change["added_fields"], [{"name": "fresh", "type": "boolean"}])
        self.assertEqual(change["removed_fields"], [{"name": "gone", "type": "integer"}])
        self.assertEqual(change["type_changes"], [
            {"name": "narrowed", "before": "number", "after": "integer"},
            {"name": "switched", "before": "string", "after": "boolean"},
            {"name": "widened", "before": "integer", "after": "number"}])
        self.assertIs(change["breaking"], True)

lines: A local registry of dataset fields and direct dependencies, requiring Python 3.10+ and no third-party packages. It records descriptions and schemas, not the dataset contents.

-`python3 dataset_catalog.py describe orders` reads the included sample catalog. `python3 dataset_catalog.py dependencies daily_totals` returns the registered orders entry; queries are direct-only, not transitive. `python3 dataset_catalog.py impact orders` reports every registered dataset reachable downstream of `orders`, each with its shortest distance and propagation path; pass `--max-depth` (a positive integer) to limit how many dependency edges are traversed. `python3 dataset_catalog.py export --id daily_totals` writes `{"datasets": [...]}` containing the selected datasets together with every upstream dataset reachable through `depends_on`; repeat `--id` to select more (duplicates merge), or omit it to export the whole catalog. Records are ordered dependencies first, breaking ties by id; exporting never modifies the catalog, and the output can be fed back to `register` entry by entry to rebuild the selected subset offline. `python3 dataset_catalog.py import FILE` imports a whole export-shaped bundle (`{"datasets": [...]}`) in one batch into the catalog selected by `--catalog`; dependencies may point at already registered datasets or at other datasets in the same batch, descriptors may appear in any order, and only metadata is registered — dataset contents are never read. Any validation failure rejects the whole batch, leaves the catalog file untouched and never creates a missing file or its parent directories; CLI errors are JSON with exit code 2. `python3 dataset_catalog.py diff FILE` performs a read-only comparison: the catalog selected by `--catalog` is the before state and the `{"datasets": [...]}` snapshot in FILE is the complete after state (a partial export still represents the whole after catalog and is not padded with current records, and records matching by id are compared directly without import's existing-id conflict rule). It prints `{"added": [...], "removed": [...], "changed": [...]}`, each array sorted by dataset id; `added` and `removed` hold full normalized records found only on one side, while each `changed` item holds `id`, `before`, `after` and a lexicographically sorted `changed_keys` list, and unchanged same-id records are omitted (empty arrays are still returned). Snapshot descriptors follow the same normalization rules as registration, so description conversion, field filtering, dependency sorting, tag cleaning and owner cleaning apply, unsaved extra properties and object key order are ignored, and tag spelling/order changes — including omitting `tags` versus `tags: []` — and owner changes (adding, removing, or changing the cleaned spelling, but not surrounding whitespace alone) count as changes, while dataset or dependency ordering alone do not. The snapshot is validated as a self-contained catalog: dependencies may use forward references but must stay inside the snapshot, and a non-object snapshot, a missing or non-array `datasets` key, an invalid descriptor, a duplicate id, a duplicate or missing dependency, a self dependency or a cycle raises `ValueError` with no partial diff; an empty snapshot means the after state has no datasets, while a missing catalog file or one containing `{}` means an empty before state. The comparison never mutates the passed bundle, the catalog file or the snapshot file, never creates files or directories, never reads dataset contents, and an unreadable file, invalid JSON or failed validation prints JSON containing `error` and exits 2. `python3 dataset_catalog.py preview FILE` is a read-only change-impact preview with the same before/after snapshot semantics as `diff`: it prints `{"diff": {...}, "affected": [...]}`, where `diff` is exactly the object `diff` prints and `affected` lists every downstream dataset reached from a change source. Added and removed records and every `changed` record are change sources — a description-only, tags-only or owner-only change propagates just like any other change — and when the diff is empty `affected` is `[]`. Each affected item (sorted by dataset id) holds only `id` and `causes`; a dataset appears once per side on which any change source reaches it along downstream edges, but a change source is never listed solely because it itself changed (it may still appear when another source reaches it). `causes` is sorted by source id and each cause holds only the source `id` plus `before` and `after`, the shortest propagation explanation on that side (positive edge `distance` and a `path` including source and target; ties choose the lexicographically smallest id sequence), or `null` when the source or target is absent or unreachable on that side; a cause with both sides `null` is omitted. The two sides are queried independently — a path valid only after the change is never stitched onto a before path — so a removed source can still affect retained or removed datasets in `before`, while an added source propagates only in `after`. Preview applies the snapshot validation of `diff` and additionally validates the current catalog's dependency graph: invalid descriptors, duplicate ids, duplicate or missing dependencies, self dependencies and cycles all raise `ValueError` with no partial result; a missing catalog file or `{}` is an empty catalog and an empty snapshot deletes every record. Preview never mutates its inputs, files or directories, never reads dataset contents, and its output does not depend on input ordering; file, JSON or validation failures print JSON containing `error` and exit 2. `python3 dataset_catalog.py apply FILE` commits the `{"datasets": [...]}` snapshot in FILE as the complete new state of the catalog selected by `--catalog`: records matching by id are replaced, new ids are added, records absent from the snapshot are removed (a partial export still represents the whole target catalog and is not padded with current records), and an empty snapshot clears the catalog. It prints the same `{"added": [...], "removed": [...], "changed": [...]}` object `diff` would have printed before the commit. The snapshot follows `diff`'s normalization and validation rules and the current catalog is validated with `preview`'s rules; any validation failure rejects the whole apply, leaves the catalog file untouched and never creates a missing file or its parent directories. The commit is all-or-nothing: when there are differences the full set of normalized records is saved atomically in the existing storage format (creating parent directories as needed), a save failure raises `OSError` with the original file contents preserved and a previously missing file still absent, and when there is no difference nothing is written or created. Pass `--expected FILE` to declare the catalog state the change was based on: FILE holds a `{"datasets": [...]}` snapshot that is validated and normalized exactly like the target snapshot and compared against the current catalog by dataset id (dataset order, object key order, unsaved properties and dependency order are ignored, while field order, tag retention/spelling/order and cleaned owner spelling count); unless the two match, the apply is rejected with `catalog does not match expected snapshot` — even when the target equals the current state — and an empty expected snapshot matches only an empty catalog. A `null` expected file is an invalid snapshot. Only metadata is handled — dataset contents are never read — and after a successful apply every query and export immediately reflects the new state. An unreadable file, invalid JSON, failed validation or a failed save prints JSON containing `error` and exits 2. `python3 dataset_catalog.py search "daily amount"` performs a read-only keyword search over dataset ids, descriptions and field names (dependency ids and field type text are not searched); the query is optional and `--field-type string|integer|number|boolean` restricts results to datasets having at least one field of that type. `--tag TAG` (repeatable, one tag per flag) restricts results to datasets carrying every given tag. `--owner OWNER` restricts results to datasets whose `owner` string matches the given value in full after Unicode casefold (surrounding Unicode whitespace is stripped first); records without an owner never match an owner filter, and the owner value is not searched by keywords. The call never mutates the bundle, catalog or snapshot file, never creates files or directories, and never reads dataset contents; the output is independent of input order. `DatasetCatalog.schema_diff_bundle(bundle)` is a read-only review of field-level changes using the same complete-before/current-and-complete-after/snapshot semantics, normalization and two-sided dependency-graph validation as `preview_bundle`: the snapshot is validated as a self-contained graph and the current catalog is validated too, so invalid descriptors, duplicate ids, duplicate or missing dependencies, self dependencies and cycles raise `ValueError` before any comparison, even when the only difference would be other metadata; a missing catalog file or `{}` is an empty catalog and an empty snapshot removes everything. It returns exactly `{"changes": [...]}`, sorted by dataset id, listing only records with field changes (no field change anywhere yields `{"changes": []}`); each item holds exactly `id`, `added_fields`, `removed_fields`, `type_changes` and `breaking`. `added_fields` and `removed_fields` hold `name`/`type` pairs and `type_changes` holds `name`/`before`/`after` pairs with the field name and its before and after types; all three arrays are sorted by field name in Unicode code-point order and are always present (as empty arrays). All fields of an added dataset count as added and all fields of a removed dataset count as removed; same-named fields are paired by their exact original names with no stripping or case folding, so a renaming is reported as one removal plus one addition. Differences limited to field order, description, tags, owner or dependencies produce no item (the field-order rule belongs only to the original `diff_bundle` comparison, which is unchanged). `breaking` is the feature's fixed verdict: `true` when at least one field is removed or at least one type change is not integer-to-number, and `false` otherwise — integer widening to number alone is therefore not breaking. The call never mutates the passed bundle or the catalog file, never creates files or directories, and never reads dataset contents; mutating the returned object affects neither the input bundle nor later queries. `DatasetCatalog.apply_bundle(bundle, expected_bundle=None)` commits a validated snapshot bundle as the complete catalog state — same-id records are replaced, new ids are added, records missing from the snapshot are removed, and an empty snapshot clears the catalog — and returns the pre-commit diff exactly as `diff_bundle` would have returned it (the `added`/`removed`/`changed` arrays sorted by id, with full before/after records and `changed_keys`). Normalization and snapshot validation match `diff_bundle`, the current catalog is validated with `preview_bundle`'s rules, and a missing catalog file or `{}` is an empty before state; any validation failure raises `ValueError` before anything is written, so the catalog file keeps its original contents and a missing file or its parent directories are never created. The commit is all-or-nothing: with differences the full set of normalized records is saved atomically in the existing storage format (parent directories are created as needed), a save failure raises `OSError` leaving the original file untouched and a previously missing file still absent, and an empty diff returns the three empty arrays without writing a file or creating directories. When `expected_bundle` is not `None` it is validated with the same snapshot rules as the target and compared against the current catalog read for this call — normalized records aligned by dataset id, ignoring dataset order, object key order, unsaved properties and dependency order, while field order, tag retention/spelling/order and cleaned owner spelling count; a mismatch raises `ValueError("catalog does not match expected snapshot")` before anything is written, even when the target equals the current state, and an empty expected snapshot matches only an empty catalog. The call never mutates the passed bundle, mutating the returned records affects neither the input nor the saved catalog, and afterwards `describe`, `dependencies`, `search`, `impact` and `export` immediately reflect the new state; existing registration, import, export, diff and preview behavior is unchanged. `DatasetCatalog.search(query="", field_type=None)` is read-only and returns a list sorted by dataset id; each item holds the same full record as `describe` under `dataset` and `matched_fields`, the field names hit by any query word in original field order without duplicates (empty when no field is hit or the query is empty). The query is split on Unicode whitespace, duplicate words do not change the result, and matching is literal substring matching after Unicode casefold — no regex or wildcards; every word must hit the same dataset, possibly across its id, description and different field names. An empty or whitespace-only query imposes no keyword restriction; when `field_type` is one of string, integer, number or boolean the dataset must have at least one field of that type while keywords still search every field name. A non-string query, or a `field_type` other than `None` and the four supported types, raises `ValueError` — arguments are validated before the catalog is read, so a missing or empty catalog still yields `[]` and never creates a file. `DatasetCatalog.search(query="", field_type=None, tags=None, owner=None)` also accepts `tags`: `None` or `[]` imposes no tag restriction, while a nonempty list requires the dataset to carry every listed tag. Tags follow the same type, stripping and dedup rules as registration, are validated before the catalog is read, and match whole tags by Unicode casefold only — no word splitting, substring, regex or wildcard matching. `owner=None` imposes no owner restriction; any other value is stripped of surrounding Unicode whitespace under the same nonempty-string rules as registration and must equal the record's stored owner in full after Unicode casefold — no word splitting, substring or wildcard matching. Records without an owner never match an owner filter; the owner filter is validated before the catalog is read. Records registered before owners existed are treated as having no owner and are never rewritten by a search. Keyword, field-type, tag and owner conditions all apply together; keywords still search only the original scopes (owner is not a keyword scope) and `matched_fields` still reflects keyword hits only. CLI errors are JSON and exit 2. Run `python3 -B -m unittest -v` for persistence, dependency validation and CLI tests.

Implementation complete. Summary of changes:

## `dataset_catalog.py`
- **`DatasetCatalog.schema_diff_bundle(bundle)`** — reuses `_snapshot_state(bundle)` (snapshot normalization + self-contained graph validation with forward references) and `_current_state()` (catalog-side validation, same as `preview`), then compares via new static helper `_schema_diff_states`:
  - Records sorted by id; only records with field changes appear; empty result is `{"changes": []}`.
  - Each item contains exactly `id`, `added_fields`, `removed_fields` (name/type pairs), `type_changes` (name/before/after), `breaking` — empty arrays always retained.
  - All three arrays sorted by field name in Unicode code-point order (plain `sorted()`).
  - Fields paired by **exact** name (no strip/casefold) — renames surface as removal + addition; field order, description, tags, owner and dependency changes produce no entry.
  - Added dataset → all fields added; removed dataset (incl. empty snapshot) → all fields removed.
  - `breaking = true` when any field is removed or any type change other than `integer → number` occurs.
  - Builds fresh dicts, so inputs and later queries are unaffected.
- **`schema-diff FILE` CLI subcommand** using the global `--catalog`, dispatched through the existing handler — `OSError` and `json.JSONDecodeError` (a `ValueError` subclass) print JSON containing `error` and exit 2; success exits 0. No files or directories are created and no data contents are read.

## Tests (`test_dataset_catalog.py`, +336 lines, 12 new cases, 95 total passing)
Cover add/remove/type-change structure, integer→number non-breaking vs. every other type change, dataset add/delete, Unicode codepoint ordering, exact-name matching and renames, metadata/field-order invisibility while confirming the original `diff` still reports field-order changes, id sorting and omission of unchanged records, missing/`{}`/empty catalog and snapshot semantics, two-sided graph validation (including a metadata-only invalid snapshot and an invalid current catalog), input/result non-mutation and no directory creation, plus a full CLI success/error test (exit 0/2, error JSON, catalog untouched).

## Docs
README.md gains a `schema-diff` CLI paragraph and a `schema_diff_bundle` API paragraph (including the fixed breaking-change rule and compatibility notes); run.txt gains the smoke-test entry.
